threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still check the Tube app like it's gospel. Real locals just swipe their Oyster and walk, knowing they'll figure it out on the go.
Last night on the 59, couple was arguing about a missing shoe. Ended with him tossing a flip flop out the window. Such a classic Brixton moment.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a group of kids playing football in a back alley while an old man serenaded us with his accordion. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a spontaneous outdoor film screening at midnight, complete with popcorn from the nearest Späti. It's such a vibe.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a local knows not to trust the BART schedule when it's a Giants game night—those special services are all hype, delays are a given.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the Muni last week packed full of tourists. One guy had a sandwich so big it didn’t fit in his lap. Everyone was sharing a laugh—classic SF moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: You'd think the street performers are all about music, but half the time they're just shouting random phrases in English to lure in the tourists.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they struggle to find the right plat de dia – asking for the English menu while locals enjoy their homemade fare.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still avoid the buskers in the Square. A true Hackneyer knows they’re just part of the scenery now.
Last night, the 133 was a circus. A guy in a clown costume kept juggling, while two others argued over the last slice of pizza. Only in Brixton!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a man at the bus stop teaching his parrot to swear in German, I realized Neukölln was home. It's those little moments that stick with you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a bar where the cocktails are served in mismatched teacups. It's like sipping a classic with a side of chaos.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a true local by their reaction to BART delays; they just shrug and keep scrolling their phone, while the newbies panic.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a guy playing the sax on the 31 just past Market. Reminded me why we endure the delays—moments of pure San Francisco magic.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think Gràcia is just another stop for tapas, but it’s the locals’ hidden corners, like Carrer de Mozart, that tell the real story.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by their stunned look at the metro map—perplexed by the bizarre lines but still trying to sound casual about taking the L1 instead of the L2.
